fields.paraphrase: Śūrasena asks Indra what Kṛtavīrya’s father did next. Indra says the son-seeking king anxiously considers childlessness after hearing the Sankaṣṭa and dūrvā accounts. Verse3 calls the dreamer Kārtavīrya, while the waking king is explicitly Kṛtavīrya in13; the name variation is retained. He dreams of his father. They embrace, unable to speak through emotion. The father takes his hand, seats him and says Nārada reported his efforts for a son, prompting the father’s visit to Brahmā. Brahmā prescribed Sankaṣṭa-caturthī and promised offspring to the royal son once the vow removes sin. The father says the book was written according to Brahmā’s instructions, gives it, and tells him to practice for a year so Siddhivināyaka will be pleased and a son will result.
